sentences.text:
The vs Unknown on 21 July, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No. 3646 of 2014

Judgement:
The appellant is 3rd respondent/Insurance company and the respondents are claim petitioner and
respondent Nos.1 and 2 in M.V.O.P.No.749 of 2009 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident
Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Ananthapur.

The appellant filed the present appeal
questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.

2.  For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim petition.
3.

The claim petitioner filed the petition under Sections 144 and 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 read with Rule 455 of the A.P. Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-
for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident that took place on 29.04.2009.
VGKR,J 4.

The brief averments in the petition filed by the petitioner are as follows:
On 29.04.2009 the petitioner was going to Tadipatri on his motor cycle bearing registration No.AP 02S 7220 along with his brother as a pillion rider and when they reached near Maddalapalli village at about 7.30 a.m., a lorry bearing registration No.AP 02W 4548 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at high speed came and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner, as a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

The police, Narpala P.S.
registered a case in Crime No.62 of 2009 against the driver of the offending lorry for the offences under Sections 337 and 338 of IPC and after completion of investigation,
they laid charge sheet.

The 1st respondent is driver, the 2nd respondent is owner and the 3rd respondent is insurer of the offending lorry, hence, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
VGKR,J 5.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 were set ex parte.
The 3rd respondent/Insurance company filed a counter by denying the manner of accident.
It is pleaded that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle by the petitioner but not the driver of the lorry and the compensation claimed is excessive.

6. Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:
The vs Unknown on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132388784/
1 1)
Whether the accident occurred on 29.04.2009 due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP 02W 4548 and caused injuries to the petitioner?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, and if so, to what amount and from which respondent?

3) To what relief?
7.
During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioner, P.W.1 was examined and Exs.A.1 to A.5 and Exs.C.1 and C.2 were marked.

On behalf of the 3rd respondent/Insurance VGKR,J company, no oral evidence was adduced, but Ex.B.1 was got marked by consent.
8.

At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry and accordingly, allowed the petition in part granting an amount of Rs.5,50,000/- towards compensation to the petitioner with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit against all the respondents.

Aggrieved against the said order,
the appellant/Insurance company preferred the present appeal.
9. Heard learned counsels for both the parties and perused the record.

10. The grounds urged by the appellant/Insurance company are that the Tribunal failed to see that the petitioner is a student and a VGKR,J non-earning person and the petitioner negligently drove the motor cycle without having any valid driving licence.

11. Now, the point for determination is:
1) Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference by this Court? and 2) To what extent?
12. POINTS 1 & 2:
The material on record clearly proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.
On appreciation of the entire material on record, the Tribunal also came to the same conclusion.
Therefore, I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the said finding given by the Tribunal.
13. Coming to the compensation, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.5,50,000/- towards compensation to the petitioner.
The evidence of P.W.2 coupled with Ex.A.2-wound certificate clearly proves that the petitioner sustained three grievous injuries.

On considering the evidence of P.W.2-doctor, who treated the petitioner, VGKR,J Ex.A.2-wound certificate, Ex.A.4-bunch of medical bills, Ex.A.5-x- rays, Ex.C.1-x-ray and Ex.C.2-case sheet of the petitioner, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.60,000/- for three grievous injuries @ Rs.20,000/- for each injury and Rs.4,69,000/- towards medical expenses.

The Tribunal further awarded an amount of Rs.6,000/-
The vs Unknown on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132388784/
2 towards loss of earnings for four months @ Rs.1,500/- p.m., Rs.10,000/- towards transport expenses, Rs.5,000/- towards extra nourishment/special diet.
By giving cogent reasons, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,50,000/-.
The material on record reveals that the petitioner suffered three grievous injuries and three surgeries were done to him and he was hospitalized for a period of four months as an inpatient.

Therefore, on considering the total facts and circumstances of the case, it is not a fit case to interfere with the findings given by the Tribunal in awarding compensation of Rs.5,50,000/- with interest @ 8% p.a. VGKR,J 14.

It is admitted by the 3rd respondent/Insurance company that the offending lorry was insured with their Insurance company under Ex.B.1-policy and the policy was also in force as on the date of accident and the driver of the offending lorry i.e., the 1 st respondent was having a valid and driving licence at the time of accident.
Therefore, all the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.

15. For the foregoing discussion, I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the findings given by the Tribunal and the impugned order is perfectly sustainable under law and it warrants no interference and the appeal is devoid of merits, therefore, it is liable to be dismissed.

16. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed, while confirming the decree and order dated 06.02.2012 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Anantapur,
in M.V.O.P.No.749 of 2009.
